statement: Planner v1 codec-selection behavior is frozen for historical fixed-chunk archives and inherited unchanged by CDC-aware v2 and cross-file v3 as their independent baseline; v4 preserves those IDs and adds a separately frozen multi-codec baseline.

Planner consumes validated plaintext Chunks plus one public profile and emits explicit TransformPlans and per-Chunk plan references before ECF serialization; it is never used by open, verify, list, inspect, explain, or unpack, which dispatch solely from recorded plans.
research_needed: Conformance test: decoder path builds/runs without planner; fuzz readers to confirm no planner invocation.

statement: Original public profile names fast, balanced, dense, extreme map to frozen planner IDs fast-v1, balanced-v1, dense-v1, extreme-v1.
fast-v1 tries Zstandard level 1 only when the deterministic probe predicts useful compression; otherwise STORE.
evidence_in_source: none; levels chosen without cited measurement
research_needed: Benchmark ratio/speed of zstd level 1 vs LZ4 and alternative levels on representative corpora.

statement: balanced-v1 tries Zstandard levels 1, 3, and 5 when the probe predicts compression, otherwise only level 1.
evidence_in_source: none; levels chosen without cited measurement
research_needed: Measure marginal gain and CPU cost of trying levels 1/3/5 on real corpora.

statement: dense-v1 tries Zstandard levels 5, 9, and 15.
evidence_in_source: none; levels chosen without cited measurement
research_needed: Measure ratio/time of levels 5/9/15 on corpora.

statement: extreme-v1 tries Zstandard levels 9, 15, 19, and 22.
evidence_in_source: none; levels chosen without cited measurement
research_needed: Measure time/memory of level 22 under a 1 MiB window cap vs gain over level 19.

statement: Every candidate is compressed on the real Chunk; search is bounded by the profile table rather than estimated.
Planner search must not depend on elapsed time, core count, available memory, filesystem order, floating point, filenames, or extensions.
research_needed: Cross-platform, cross-core-count reproducibility test producing byte-identical archives; audit for thread- or CPU-feature-dependent codec output.

statement: The compression probe samples at most 4,096 deterministically spaced bytes and uses integer symbol-diversity, maximum-frequency, and adjacent-repeat measures; this doc does not state the thresholds.
refines_or_supersedes: Thresholds stated in docs/codec-transform-v1.md §Frozen v4 creation policies L89-93
evidence_in_source: none; sample size chosen without cited measurement
research_needed: Measure probe false-negative rate (compressible data predicted incompressible) on corpora.

statement: Inputs shorter than 64 bytes always use STORE.
Zstandard is selected only if encoded bytes + 16 bytes plan cost + max(32 bytes, ceil(1% of plaintext)) is strictly less than plaintext bytes.
refines_or_supersedes: Replaced for v4 by exact TransformPlan record bytes and STORE-complete-cost margin in docs/codec-transform-v1.md §Complete-cost rule L102-115
research_needed: Measure whether the 16-byte charge approximates actual per-plan container overhead.

statement: The smallest qualifying candidate wins and STORE wins all ties.

The fixed 16-byte charge prevents considering payload size in isolation and thresholds reject negligible savings; explicitly not a promise that every surrounding container byte is attributed to an individual Chunk.
research_needed: Quantify unattributed container overhead vs attributed plan charge on real archives.

statement: Zstandard plans use codec id zstandard/v1, 1 MiB window, content size in frame, no checksum, no dictionary identifier, no long-distance matching.
research_needed: Measure ratio loss from 1 MiB window cap and no-LDM on large chunks (fast policy max chunk 8 MiB).
decision_needed: Should a larger-window or LDM Zstandard variant be registered for large-chunk profiles?

statement: Decoder enforces the plan's 1 MiB window; archive declares a conservative 4 MiB Zstandard working-set requirement; STORE (store/v1) declares zero decoder memory.
research_needed: Measure actual zstd decoder peak memory for 1 MiB window to validate the 4 MiB declaration.

statement: Planner v3 aggregate working-set declarations may additionally include stored Dictionary bytes and bounded-group access costs.
LAI, ContentObject logical digests, and AUX exclude creation policy and codec parameters.
Under ecf/bootstrap-v1, PCR binds plaintext Chunk organization and the chunker but excludes TransformPlans, so changing only codec profile with fixed chunking preserves PCR.
Public v2 and v3 profiles may select different CDC policies, in which case PCR differs across profiles for identical content.
decision_needed: Is profile-dependent PCR acceptable for users comparing archives of the same content made with different profiles?

statement: PCI hashes every exact container byte and therefore captures planner, plan, chunking, and encoded-payload differences.

Doc states current public profiles create *-v4 archives; v3 preserves independent selection before complete-cost Dictionary and ChunkGroup choices; v4 broadens the independent baseline and retains v3 cross-file strategy.
refines_or_supersedes: Stale: docs/jpeg-reconstruction-v1.md defines v6 planners; crates/entrybound/src/planner.rs:87-90 returns *-v6 ids and README.md:46-47 names v6 as current
research_needed: Update planner-v1.md: current public planner IDs are *-v6.

statement: Later planner generations must not redefine earlier planner behavior; no v1, v2, or v3 planner behavior was redefined.
research_needed: Golden-archive regression tests per planner ID across dependency upgrades (zstd, lz4_flex, lzma-rust2, preflate-rs, jixel).
decision_needed: How is byte-identical reproduction of frozen planner IDs guaranteed when pinned codec crates must be upgraded (e.g., security fixes)?

statement: Normalized CDC and exact deduplication are frozen creation-time behavior introduced by planner v2 and inherited unchanged by planner v3 and v4.
Decoders do not implement or invoke the chunker; they consume ordered Chunk references recorded in each ContentObject.
New archives use gear-norm-v1, a normalized Gear-hash content-defined chunker.

gear-norm-v1 chosen for deterministic integer-only linear scanning, bounded state, practical insertion/deletion re-synchronization, and simple normalized distribution; small insertion does not shift later boundaries; every byte updates the hash (no boundary skipping).
research_needed: Measure dedup ratio and boundary-shift resilience vs FastCDC/Rabin/buzhash on edit-sequence corpora; note mask uses low-order hash bits whose effective window is only b+1 bytes, evaluate boundary distribution on low-entropy/repetitive data.
decision_needed: Is gear-norm-v1 (low-bit masks, normalization level 1) the right long-term CDC, or should a v2 chunker be specified?

statement: The 256-entry u64 Gear table is frozen: table[i] = splitmix64(0x6a09e667f3bcc909 + i) with standard splitmix64 constants 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15, 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9, 0x94d049bb133111eb and shifts 30/27/31.
research_needed: Independent reimplementation test vector for the table and chunk boundaries.

statement: All operations wrap modulo 2^64; from each Chunk boundary every byte updates hash = (hash << 1) + table[byte].
No boundary before minimum; with power-of-two target and b=log2(target), cut in [min,target-1] when low b+1 bits are zero, in [target,max-1] when low b-1 bits are zero, and force a cut at maximum.
research_needed: Measure resulting chunk-size distribution per policy; confirm forced-cut frequency on incompressible and zero-filled data.

statement: Mask rule is defined only for a power-of-two target; doc does not state behavior or validation for non-power-of-two targets or min/max constraints in chunker_id parsing.
research_needed: Check chunker_id validation code rejects non-power-of-two targets and min>target or target>max.
decision_needed: Must readers/validators reject chunker_id strings with non-power-of-two target or inconsistent min/target/max?

statement: Stronger early mask suppresses undersized chunks; weaker late mask encourages a boundary after target, normalizing size variance.
research_needed: Empirical chunk-size histogram vs unnormalized Gear.

statement: A final trailing region smaller than minimum is still emitted; a non-empty file is covered exactly once with no gaps or overlaps; a zero-length ContentObject has no Chunks.
research_needed: Property tests for exact coverage and zero-length handling.

statement: chunker_id records algorithm and parameters as gear-norm-v1/min-{bytes}/target-{bytes}/max-{bytes}.
v3 and current v4 policies reuse the same ordered v2 CDC candidates without altering any gear-norm-v1 parameter set.
refines_or_supersedes: Inherited again by v5 (docs/reconstructive-transform-v1.md L81-82) and v6 (docs/jpeg-reconstruction-v1.md L97-98)

statement: fast-v2 uses single CDC policy 512 KiB / 2 MiB / 8 MiB (min/target/max), coarse to minimize frame and Index churn.
research_needed: Measure dedup/ratio/index-size tradeoffs of 2 MiB target vs alternatives; interaction with 1 MiB zstd window on 8 MiB chunks.

statement: balanced-v2 uses single general-purpose CDC policy 128 KiB / 512 KiB / 2 MiB.
research_needed: Benchmark vs restic/borg/casync typical targets on backup corpora.

statement: dense-v2 considers balanced policy and 64 KiB / 256 KiB / 1 MiB, selecting lowest complete estimated physical cost.
extreme-v2 considers fast, balanced, dense, and 32 KiB / 128 KiB / 512 KiB, selecting lowest cost across the bounded full candidate set.
research_needed: Measure time cost of chunking whole input four times for extreme.

statement: CDC candidate order breaks cost ties, preferring the coarser policy.
CDC policy cost estimate = unique plaintext Chunk bytes + 164 bytes per unique Chunk (64-byte frame + 100-byte Index record) + 40 bytes per canonical manifest Chunk reference.
research_needed: Verify 64-byte frame, 100-byte Index record, and 40-byte manifest reference against actual ECF encodings, including v3 version-2 frames that append a 32-byte group_ref.
decision_needed: Should frozen estimate constants be reconciled with actual record sizes in later generations?

statement: CDC policy selection estimates cost from unique plaintext bytes before codec selection, so compressibility differences between chunkings are not considered; codec selection runs once afterwards on the chosen set.
research_needed: Measure how often compressed-size-aware policy selection would choose a different CDC policy and the ratio lost.
decision_needed: Should future planners select CDC policy on compressed complete cost rather than plaintext estimate?

statement: Identical ContentObjects are counted once in manifest-reference cost; this prevents smaller chunks winning merely by creating more dedup hits.
research_needed: Validate on corpora with many duplicate files.

statement: After CDC selection, codec selection runs once on the selected unique Chunk set with unchanged v1 STORE/Zstandard levels and minimum-gain rule.
refines_or_supersedes: Reuses docs/planner-v1.md L13-41

statement: Every Chunk receives SHA-256 over exact plaintext; ContentStore is a deterministic digest-keyed map so repeated positions, files, and ContentObjects reference one stored Chunk.
A digest collision with different captured bytes is a typed failure; similarity is never proof of equality.
research_needed: Confirm writer compares bytes (not only digest) on dedup hit, and the cost of retaining bytes for comparison.

statement: Chunk-reference order remains authoritative for reconstruction.
ContentObject logical_digest, Entry identity, and LAI are over logical plaintext and independent of Chunk boundaries; AUX remains metadata/fidelity identity.
PCR binds ContentObject chunk roots, unique Chunk count, and chunker_id, so it changes when chunking changes; PCI changes with exact ECF bytes.
Resource declarations keep total logical file bytes separate from unique physical Chunk bytes so duplicate references cannot evade caller logical-output limits.
research_needed: Fuzz/adversarial test: archive with massive duplicate references vs caller output limits.

statement: inspect and explain report both logical references and unique physical storage.

ecf/bootstrap-v1 already carried ordered Chunk references and arbitrary logical lengths, so CDC needed no ECF wire change; historical fixed-1mib/v1 and *-v1 archives still open and verify without reinterpretation.
research_needed: Golden historical-archive corpus tests.

statement: Planner v3 adds similarity clustering, optional physical reordering, Dictionaries, and bounded ChunkGroups without changing this chunker.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/cross-file-compression-v1.md

statement: STREAM layout is unsupported in the CDC generation.
decision_needed: Is STREAM layout required for v1 and how does it interact with dedup and CDC?

statement: Cross-archive deduplication is unsupported.
decision_needed: Is cross-archive dedup (incremental/base-chain archives) in scope for v1 or post-v1?

statement: Keyed/encrypted CDC boundaries are unsupported; boundaries are computed from a public unkeyed Gear table.
research_needed: Security analysis of chunk-size fingerprinting leakage under encryption with unkeyed CDC; evaluate keyed Gear table and padding.
decision_needed: Must encrypted archives use keyed CDC boundaries or padding before encryption ships?

statement: Cross-file compression intelligence is frozen creation-time behavior for planner v3.
Readers decode only the recorded Dictionary, TransformPlan, ChunkGroup, and physical Chunk order; they never run similarity analysis or the planner.
Similarity runs after CDC and exact SHA-256 deduplication, over unique plaintext Chunks in digest order.

bottom-k-shingle-v1 hashes overlapping 32-byte shingles at 16-byte stride with FNV-1a-64 (offset cbf29ce484222325, prime 00000100000001b3), scans at most 4,096 shingles per Chunk, and keeps lexicographically lowest unique hashes as a fixed-size integer-only sketch.
evidence_in_source: none; shingle size, stride, and 4,096 cap chosen without cited measurement
research_needed: Measure clustering recall/precision vs MinHash/SimHash alternatives; 4,096 shingles at 16-byte stride covers only ~65 KiB of each Chunk, evaluate effect on large chunks.

statement: Only the first ~4,096 shingles per Chunk are scanned; the doc does not say whether shingles are sampled across the whole Chunk or taken from the start, so similarity for large Chunks may reflect only a prefix.
research_needed: Inspect implementation and measure clustering quality on Chunks larger than 64 KiB.
decision_needed: Should the sketch sample spread across the full Chunk in a future similarity version?

statement: Chunks join a bounded leader cohort when sketch intersection reaches the profile threshold; candidate leaders come from sketch-value buckets; greatest intersection wins and cohort digest breaks ties.
research_needed: Specify leader-selection and bucket-scan order precisely enough for an independent reimplementation to reproduce cohorts.

statement: SHA-256, not a similarity fingerprint, is the sole authority for exact equality; similarity is neither stored as identity nor needed to decode.

The doc does not define what 'candidate cap' bounds, whether cohorts below the cohort minimum are discarded, or how Chunks exceeding the cohort maximum are handled; precise semantics are needed for independent reproduction.
research_needed: Inspect planner implementation and document cohort acceptance, overflow, and candidate-cap semantics; worst-case planning complexity analysis.

statement: fast-v3 disables similarity (no cohorts, candidate cap 0).
balanced-v3 similarity: sketch 8, threshold 500 per thousand, cohort min 8 / max 32, candidate cap 64.
research_needed: Sweep sketch size/threshold/cohort bounds on corpora to measure ratio and planning time.

statement: dense-v3 similarity: sketch 16, threshold 375 per thousand, cohort min 4 / max 64, candidate cap 128.
research_needed: Parameter sweep on corpora.

statement: extreme-v3 similarity: sketch 32, threshold 250 per thousand, cohort min 3 / max 128, candidate cap 256.
research_needed: Parameter sweep; worst-case planning time with adversarial many-similar inputs.

statement: v3 profiles retain exactly the v2 CDC candidate policies and frozen v1 independent STORE/Zstandard selection.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/chunking-v1.md L57-75; docs/planner-v1.md L13-41

statement: balanced-v3 dictionary search: levels 3 and 5; training cap 16 samples of 16 KiB each producing an 8 KiB dictionary; no lookback.
research_needed: Measure dictionary gain vs sample count/size and dictionary size.

statement: dense-v3: dictionary levels 5/9/15, 32 samples of 32 KiB, 16 KiB dictionary; lookback candidates 1, 2, 4 at levels 5 and 9.
research_needed: Measure ratio and access cost of lookback 1/2/4.

statement: extreme-v3: dictionary levels 9/15/19, 64 samples of 64 KiB, 32 KiB dictionary; lookback candidates 1, 2, 4, 8 at levels 9, 15, 19.
research_needed: Measure ratio and access cost of lookback up to 8.

statement: balanced-v3 has lookback zero by contract; every Chunk is independently decodable given its optional Dictionary.
A Dictionary is a first-class physical object with SHA-256 identity over exact bytes, codec zstandard/v1, format zstd-trained/v1, and a frozen construction identifier.
Dictionary samples are selected in Chunk-digest order, truncated to the profile cap, and trained through pinned zstd crate 0.13.3 (upstream Zstandard 1.5.7).
research_needed: Verify zstd dictionary training output is byte-deterministic across OS/CPU/thread count; zstd crate wraps native C libzstd, check consistency with pure-Rust/no-native claims elsewhere.
decision_needed: How will planner v3+ reproducibility survive a required zstd upgrade that changes trainer output?

statement: Dictionary bytes are stored once and referenced by TransformPlans; they are never duplicated inside a plan.

Dictionary candidate cost includes all encoded cohort payloads, exact canonical Dictionary record length, 64-byte section header, and exact TransformPlan record length; it must beat best independent payload cost by more than 128 bytes; simpler independent representation wins ties.
research_needed: Compare absolute 128-byte margin with v4 max(32,1%) and v5/v6 max(256,2%) rules; measure decode-cost impact of marginal dictionary wins.
decision_needed: Should gain thresholds be harmonized across planner generations?

statement: The 64-byte section header is charged per dictionary candidate cohort; the doc does not state whether it is charged once per archive or repeatedly for each cohort.
research_needed: Inspect planner implementation for header charge accounting.

statement: Dictionary training failure is a normal rejected candidate, not an archive error.
Dense and extreme may instead select a Zstandard reference-prefix plan; a ChunkGroup stores only stable identifier, max_lookback, and exact worst-case max_preceding_bytes.
Group membership authority exists only in each Chunk's group_ref; consecutive CHUNK_DATA frame order is the authority for dependency order; ChunkGroup never duplicates a member list.

To decode a dependent Chunk, the reader decodes up to max_lookback preceding Chunks in the same contiguous group, concatenates their plaintext in physical order, and supplies the final 1 MiB as Zstandard reference prefix; the first Chunk has empty prefix.

Doc does not state whether preceding Chunks' own prefixes are required transitively; if each preceding Chunk is itself dependent, true decode cost could extend to group start rather than max_lookback Chunks.
research_needed: Inspect encoder/decoder to confirm whether prefixes are built from transitively decoded plaintext and whether max_preceding_bytes accounts for it; adversarial access-cost tests.
decision_needed: Is declared access cost defined over direct or transitive dependencies, and is it a guaranteed upper bound?

statement: Only the final 1 MiB of concatenated preceding plaintext is used, yet up to 8 preceding Chunks (possibly multi-MiB each) must be decoded; efficiency of lookback 8 with large Chunks is not analyzed.
research_needed: Measure decode work vs ratio gain for lookback 4/8 when chunks exceed 1 MiB.

statement: Lookback uses the safe Zstandard reference-prefix API with no hidden persistent compressor state and no unsafe Rust in Entrybound.
research_needed: Audit: zstd crate binds native C libzstd via zstd-sys, so safety claim is limited to Entrybound's own code; confirm #![forbid(unsafe_code)].

statement: Lookback planner charges encoded payloads, exact plan and group record lengths, and the 64-byte group-section header, with the same strict 128-byte cohort gain rule.

Declared access bytes equal maximum sum of full logical lengths of preceding required Chunks; open and verify recompute it, enforce contiguity and bounds, and aggregate it into the archive decoder working-set requirement.
research_needed: Fuzz ChunkGroup records with false max_preceding_bytes and non-contiguous members.

statement: Accepted similarity cohorts are physically contiguous in cohort-ID order; remaining unique Chunks follow in digest order.
research_needed: Measure effect of digest-order layout on streaming/locality vs original file order (HTTP range fetch count).
decision_needed: Is digest-order physical layout acceptable for sequential extraction and remote access performance?

statement: ContentObject Chunk-reference order and canonical Entry order never change due to physical reordering.

Physical reordering, dictionaries, codec parameters, and group layout do not enter ContentObject logical digests, LAI, AUX, or current PCR; with unchanged boundaries and metadata those identities stay unchanged while PCI may change.
The experimental namespace remains ecf/bootstrap-v1, extended by required incompatibility feature bit 0x0000_0000_0000_0001 named cross-file-compression-v1.
decision_needed: When does the experimental ecf/bootstrap-v1 namespace become a stable, long-term-supported format?

statement: Extended archive canonical section order: DESCRIPTOR, TRANSFORM_PLANS, DICTIONARIES, CHUNK_GROUPS, CHUNK_DATA, MANIFEST_RECORDS, FIDELITY, optional INDEX.
refines_or_supersedes: Extended by v6 order in docs/jpeg-reconstruction-v1.md L170-172

statement: Dictionary record type 11 contains identity, codec, format, construction, bytes; ChunkGroup record type 12 contains identifier, max lookback, max preceding bytes.
Extended version-2 Chunk frames append the sole 32-byte group_ref authority to the historical header; a zero digest means no group.
All-zero group_ref is a sentinel for no group; doc does not state that a ChunkGroup identifier can never be the zero digest or that such a record is rejected.
research_needed: Check validator rejects ChunkGroup id equal to zero digest.

statement: New readers retain the historical section schema and version-1 Chunk frames for *-v1/*-v2 archives; historical readers see the unknown required feature and fail closed.
Missing, duplicate, corrupt, unsupported, or mismatched dictionaries and invalid group references, ordering, lookback, or access costs produce stable typed diagnostics.
research_needed: Negative conformance corpus enumerating each diagnostic.

statement: Planner v3 does not add content-specific parsers or additional codecs.
refines_or_supersedes: Later added: codecs in docs/codec-transform-v1.md (v4); parsers in docs/reconstructive-transform-v1.md (v5) and docs/jpeg-reconstruction-v1.md (v6)

statement: Unbounded solid compression and cross-archive dictionaries are not supported.
research_needed: Measure ratio gap vs 7z/tar.xz solid mode on many-small-file corpora.
decision_needed: Is bounded ChunkGroup lookback sufficient to be competitive with solid archivers, or is a bounded-solid mode needed?

statement: STREAM layout, encryption, and remote retrieval are not added by cross-file compression v1.
Codec and structural-transform generation v1 is an experimental frozen implementation note for v4 planners; it extends ecf/bootstrap-v1 and does not redefine v1-v3 archive bytes.
decision_needed: What does 'experimental frozen' commit to: will v4 archives be readable indefinitely by future releases?

statement: Codec and transform identifiers are matched only against compile-time registries.

Each registry entry owns identifier, format version, required incompatibility feature, parameter validation, deterministic encode/decode dispatch, and decoder-resource derivation; transform entries also own reversibility class and forward/inverse operations.
Archive-controlled strings cannot select arbitrary executable code.
research_needed: Fuzz TransformPlan identifiers/parameters; review for dynamic dispatch paths.

statement: V4 archives require incompatibility bit 0x2 named codec-transform-v1 in addition to v3's cross-file-compression-v1 (0x1).
With bit 0x2, TransformPlan field 3 contains ordered canonical type-13 TransformStep records with fields transform identifier (1) and canonical parameter bytes (2).
Both TransformStep fields are required; unknown identifiers, duplicate transform families, or invalid parameters fail closed.
research_needed: Negative corpus for each failure; define 'transform family' precisely.

statement: Without bit 0x2 the historical TransformPlan transform field must remain empty; the gate avoids assigning new meaning to the old placeholder, which released planners never populated.
store/v1 has empty parameters and no decoder requirement.
zstandard/v1 parameters are frozen ZP01, ZD01, or ZX01 records from v1/v3, declaring 1 MiB window and 4 MiB working set.
research_needed: Document ZP01/ZD01/ZX01 layouts in a normative spec; measure decoder memory.

statement: lz4/v1 parameters are 'L401', block format 1, three zero reserved bytes; declared 64 KiB window and 128 KiB working set.
lzma2/v1 parameters are 'LM21', preset u8, three zero flag/reserved bytes, dictionary bytes u32be; declares recorded dictionary window and lzma2_get_memory_usage(dict) * 1024 working set.
research_needed: Verify lzma2_get_memory_usage formula matches actual lzma-rust2 decoder allocation; check archive-supplied dictionary sizes are bounded before use.

statement: LZ4 is a raw independent block encoded by pinned lz4_flex 0.14.0 with its safe default block encoder; no frame defaults or external dictionary are implicit.
research_needed: Confirm lz4_flex block output is stable across patch versions; independent LZ4 block decoders interoperate.

statement: LZMA2 is a raw independent stream encoded by pinned lzma-rust2 0.20.0 with default features disabled and only std plus encoder enabled.
refines_or_supersedes: Doc drift: crates/entrybound/Cargo.toml:29 also enables the 'xz' feature
research_needed: Reconcile documented feature set with Cargo.toml (xz feature enabled).

statement: LZMA2 frozen (preset, dictionary) pairs are (4, 1 MiB), (6, 4 MiB), (9, 8 MiB); chunk size automatic, single-threaded, no external dictionary.
evidence_in_source: none; pairs chosen without cited measurement
research_needed: Measure ratio/time/memory of each pair; confirm 'automatic chunk size' is deterministic across platforms.

statement: Selected codec crates are permissively licensed (MIT lz4_flex, Apache-2.0 lzma-rust2); Entrybound contains no unsafe codec implementation.
research_needed: cargo-deny/license audit; unsafe audit of dependencies (lz4_flex, lzma-rust2, zstd-sys native).

statement: Decoder validates full parameter value and caller memory policy before dispatch, allocates only the declared logical output length, rejects trailing/malformed payloads and length mismatch, then applies inverse transforms and verifies authoritative plaintext Chunk SHA-256.
research_needed: Fuzz each codec decoder with malformed and trailing payloads; memory ceiling tests.

statement: All v1 structural transforms are length-preserving bijections over every byte string.
research_needed: Property tests for round-trip over arbitrary lengths including empty.

statement: delta8/v1 has empty parameters; forward byte i = input[i] - previous mod 256 with previous starting 0; inverse cumulatively adds modulo 256.

byte-shuffle/v1 parameter is one byte of value 2, 4, or 8; forward emits lane 0..w-1 over floor(length/w) complete records, copying the final length mod w bytes unchanged; inverse restores interleaving.
Encoding applies TransformSteps in recorded order then the codec; decoding runs codec decode then inverse steps in reverse order.

V4 retains v3 CDC, exact dedup, similarity, dictionary, physical ordering, and bounded lookback; balanced-v4 still has lookback zero by contract; independent candidate sets are ordered and earlier simpler candidates win equal complete cost.
fast-v4 independent candidates: STORE, LZ4, Zstandard level 1; no structural candidates.
Doc does not state whether fast-v4 still gates Zstandard level 1 on the v1 compression probe as fast-v1 did, or always tries STORE, LZ4, and Zstandard 1.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/planner-v1.md Profile table L17
research_needed: Inspect planner.rs v4 fast path.

statement: balanced-v4 candidates: STORE, LZ4, Zstandard 1/3/5; structural: delta8 then Zstandard 3, byte-shuffle-4 then Zstandard 3.
dense-v4 candidates: STORE, Zstandard 5/9/15, LZMA2 4+1MiB, LZMA2 6+4MiB (no LZ4); structural: delta8 and byte-shuffle-2/4/8 each with Zstandard 9 and LZMA2 6+4MiB.
research_needed: Explain why dense excludes LZ4 while extreme includes it; measure LZ4 win frequency.

statement: extreme-v4 candidates: STORE, LZ4, Zstandard 9/15/19/22, all three LZMA2 pairs; structural: delta8 and byte-shuffle-2/4/8 each with Zstandard 15, LZMA2 6+4MiB, and LZMA2 9+8MiB.
research_needed: Measure planning time: up to 20+ encodes per Chunk.

statement: Structural eligibility probe is the existing v1 probe: search runs if distinct bytes in sample are at most 192, most common byte reaches 12,000 ppm, or adjacent equal bytes reach 20,000 ppm.
refines_or_supersedes: Specifies thresholds for probe described in docs/planner-v1.md L24-26
research_needed: Measure how often structural transforms would win on chunks the probe rejects.

statement: Fast never searches transforms; the probe only bounds work and actual candidate bytes decide selection.

After independent selection, the unchanged v3 strategy may replace a similarity cohort with shared-dictionary Zstandard (balanced, dense, extreme) or bounded prefix lookback (dense, extreme), with full Dictionary/ChunkGroup costs in the comparison.
Dictionary and lookback representations do not accept structural transforms in this generation.
research_needed: Measure potential gain of delta/shuffle combined with dictionary or prefix compression.
decision_needed: Should a future planner allow structural transforms before dictionary/lookback encoding?

statement: Independent candidate cost is exact encoded payload bytes plus exact canonical TransformPlan record bytes.
refines_or_supersedes: Refines docs/planner-v1.md Win rule L29-35 (replaces fixed 16-byte charge)

statement: TransformPlan records may be shared by many Chunks; doc does not state whether the plan record cost is charged per Chunk or once, which affects selection for common plans.
research_needed: Inspect planner cost accounting for shared TransformPlans.

statement: Non-STORE candidates must improve on STORE by more than max(32 bytes, 1% of STORE complete cost); a structural pipeline must clear that same margin against the best non-transform candidate; strict comparison makes STORE and simpler candidates win ties.
Dictionary and group selection continue to include payloads, full Dictionary/TransformPlan/group records, and section overhead as for v3.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/cross-file-compression-v1.md L52-57, L74-76

statement: Codec identifiers and parameters, TransformSteps, Dictionary choice, ChunkGroup layout, and physical ordering are physical facts that do not enter ContentObject logical digest, LAI, AUX, or PCR; exact container PCI may change.
Codec-transform v1 introduces no format-specific parser, reconstructive transform, executable transform, new CDC algorithm, unbounded solid stream, encryption, or STREAM layout.
refines_or_supersedes: Reconstructive transforms later added by docs/reconstructive-transform-v1.md (v5)

statement: Executable (archive-supplied program) transforms are excluded; only registered fixed transforms may run.
Reconstructive transform v1 is an experimental frozen implementation note for v5 planners.

Entrybound pins Microsoft preflate-rs 0.7.6 for bit-exact DEFLATE reconstruction because it is Apache-2.0, forbids unsafe Rust, exposes exact stream recreation, and accepts explicit plaintext and hash-chain bounds.
research_needed: Verify preflate-rs forbids unsafe including transitive deps; assess maintenance/longevity risk and determinism of correction data across versions.
decision_needed: What is the long-term plan if preflate-rs is abandoned, given archives depend on its exact correction format for decode?

statement: preflate-rs requires Rust 1.89, so Entrybound MSRV became 1.89.
refines_or_supersedes: Superseded by docs/jpeg-reconstruction-v1.md L11 (MSRV 1.94); Cargo.toml:8 rust-version 1.94

statement: crc32fast 1.5.0 validates gzip payload checksums; flate2 1.1.9 is test-only for fixture generation.
Entrybound does not implement a DEFLATE parser; archive strings dispatch only through the governed transform registry.
delta8/v1 and byte-shuffle/v1 are classed Structural: accept every byte string, preserve length, invertible by construction.
deflate-reconstruct/v1 is classed Reconstructive: format-specific, length-changing, and requires side data.
A v5 pipeline has at most one reconstructive step, which must be first in forward order, followed by zero or more Structural steps; the codec remains last.
research_needed: Negative tests for pipelines with reconstructive step not first or repeated.

statement: Inverse decoding runs codec, reverses Structural steps, reconstructs original DEFLATE bytes, then verifies original plaintext Chunk length and SHA-256 digest.

V1 attempts only a complete Chunk containing raw DEFLATE fully consumed and exactly recreated by preflate, zlib (DEFLATE method, valid header, no preset dictionary, valid Adler-32), or one gzip member (bounded valid header, DEFLATE, valid CRC-32 and ISIZE).

Eligibility requires the stream to be exactly one complete CDC Chunk, but CDC splits files larger than the policy minimum; doc does not analyze how many real gzip/zlib files are eligible; the 16 MiB input limit exceeds every CDC maximum used by recognizing profiles (2 MiB or less for balanced/dense).
research_needed: Measure fraction of DEFLATE streams in realistic corpora that land as a single complete Chunk under each CDC policy, and resulting savings.
decision_needed: Should DEFLATE reconstruction adopt v6-style whole-ContentObject regions?

statement: V1 does not scan PNG, ZIP, arbitrary embedded regions, concatenated gzip members, or streams crossing Chunk boundaries.
research_needed: Measure recompression gain available from PNG/ZIP/multi-member gzip/embedded streams in target corpora.
decision_needed: Which container-embedded DEFLATE sources (PNG IDAT, ZIP members, PDF, docx) should a later reconstructive version support?

statement: A failed or ambiguous reconstruction attempt falls back to the ordinary v4-compatible candidates.
For every candidate the writer runs original -> preflate plaintext + corrections -> recreated and requires both SHA-256 equality and byte-for-byte equality.
The native ECF writer repeats reconstruction against recorded side data so callers cannot commit an unverified reconstructive EAM; this check cannot be disabled.
research_needed: Test that API paths injecting precomputed plans are still verified.

statement: Write-time exact recreation implies decode-time recreation will succeed on any platform and future build; this relies on preflate-rs decoding being deterministic and stable.
research_needed: Cross-platform decode tests of stored ReconstructionData; archive golden corpus across preflate-rs upgrades.

statement: ReconstructionData is physical, digest-addressed by SHA-256 of exact bytes, stored once, referenced by TransformStep v2, and records format preflate-rs-0.7.6/deflate-reconstruct-v1 plus intermediate length.
The ReconstructionData format identifier embeds the preflate-rs crate version, binding archive decode to a specific library version's correction format.
research_needed: Determine whether newer preflate-rs versions decode 0.7.6 corrections identically.
decision_needed: Must future builds retain preflate-rs 0.7.6 (or a compatible reimplementation) forever to decode v5 archives?

statement: ReconstructionData bytes: 'ERD1' | wrapper u8 | 3 reserved bytes | prefix_length u32be | correction_length u64be | suffix_length u32be | prefix | preflate corrections | suffix.
research_needed: Fuzz ERD1 parser for length overflow and reserved-byte validation.

statement: Wrapper values raw=0, zlib=1, gzip=2; prefix and suffix preserve exact container bytes and correction stream recreates exact raw DEFLATE body.

Feature bit 0x4 requires bits 0x1 and 0x2, adds canonical record type 14 (ReconstructionData) and TransformStep v2 record type 15, and selects section sequence documented in format-v0.md; historical type-13 steps and v1-v4 sections unchanged.
refines_or_supersedes: Section sequence delegated to docs/format-v0.md

statement: The ReconstructionData section may contain canonical type-16 ReconstructionFallback audit records after all ReconstructionData objects, associating a Chunk digest with unrecognized-or-verification-failed or complete-cost-rejected.
refines_or_supersedes: Extended by type-19 ReconstructionAudit v2 in docs/jpeg-reconstruction-v1.md L167-168

statement: Fallback records are non-authoritative physical planning evidence, carry no alternate Chunk meaning, and participate only in section integrity and PCI.
Persisting type-16 fallback audits in every archive discloses which Chunks contain DEFLATE-like data and costs bytes; doc does not discuss privacy or whether audits can be omitted.
research_needed: Measure audit record overhead; assess leakage under encryption (whether audit records are inside encrypted records).
decision_needed: Should planning audit records be optional or excluded from encrypted/minimal archives?

statement: All v5 profiles retain corresponding frozen v4 candidates, CDC, deduplication, similarity, Dictionary, and bounded-group behavior.
fast-v5 performs no DEFLATE recognition and has no reconstructive candidates; lookback remains zero.
balanced-v5 recognizes complete bounded streams with max chain 512; candidates reconstruction then Zstandard levels 3 and 5; lookback zero.
research_needed: Measure reconstruction success rate and time vs preflate max chain setting.

statement: dense-v5 recognizes with max chain 2048; candidates reconstruction then Zstandard 9, LZMA2 preset 6 / 4 MiB, or delta8 then Zstandard 9.
extreme-v5 recognizes with max chain 4096; candidates reconstruction then Zstandard 15/19, LZMA2 preset 9 / 8 MiB, delta8 then Zstandard 15, byte-shuffle 2/4/8 then LZMA2 preset 9 / 8 MiB.

Reconstructive candidate cost = encoded payload + canonical TransformPlan v2 + canonical ReconstructionData record + 64 bytes section framing; it must beat best ordinary v4 representation by strictly more than both 256 bytes and 2%; ordinary encoding wins ties.
research_needed: Justify stricter 256-byte/2% margin (vs 32/1% for v4) by measuring decode CPU cost of reconstruction.

statement: The base of the 2% margin is not stated (best ordinary v4 cost, original plaintext, or STORE cost).
research_needed: Inspect planner.rs v5 margin computation and document it.

statement: Existing cohort planning then compares its full Dictionary/lookback cost against the independent (possibly reconstructive) result.

explain reads persisted type-16 records to report every non-selected v5 attempt as fallback, split into recognition/verification failures and complete-cost rejections, and reports selected gross payload savings, ReconstructionData overhead, and net savings.

V1 limits original input and ReconstructionData to 16 MiB each, intermediate plaintext to 64 MiB, expansion to 64x, and declares an additional 80 MiB working set on every selected reconstructive plan.
evidence_in_source: none; limits chosen without cited measurement
research_needed: Measure actual preflate-rs peak memory for 16 MiB inputs to validate 80 MiB declaration; decompression-bomb tests at 64x.

statement: Caller archive and decode policies are checked before payload decoding; lengths are checked before allocation where available; wrapper parsing is bounded; malformed state uses reconstructive-specific typed diagnostics.
research_needed: Identify code paths where lengths cannot be checked before allocation inside preflate-rs; fuzz.

statement: Original pre-transform bytes remain Chunk plaintext identity; ReconstructionData, transform parameters, and codecs do not enter ContentObject identity, LAI, AUX, or PCR; with unchanged chunking and metadata only PCI changes.
JPEG whole-object reconstruction (jpeg-jxl-reconstruct/v1) is an experimental frozen implementation note for v6 planners.
Entrybound uses pure-Rust jixel 0.2.19 encoder and jxl-oxide 0.12.6 decoder/reconstructor, both with default features disabled.
research_needed: Assess maturity/maintenance of jixel 0.2.x (pre-1.0) and longevity risk for archives whose decode depends on jxl-oxide reconstruction.
decision_needed: Is depending on a 0.2.x JPEG XL encoder acceptable for a frozen archive format feature?

statement: jixel is BSD-3-Clause OR Apache-2.0 and jxl-oxide is MIT OR Apache-2.0.
No GPL component, native library, subprocess, or external command is part of core decoding.
research_needed: Verify with cargo tree: zstd 0.13.3 crate (crates/entrybound/Cargo.toml:41) wraps native C libzstd via zstd-sys, which appears to contradict a no-native-library claim for core decoding unless scoped to JPEG only.
decision_needed: Is a native C Zstandard library acceptable in core decoding, or must a pure-Rust decoder be used?

statement: jixel raises workspace MSRV to Rust 1.94.
refines_or_supersedes: Supersedes MSRV 1.89 in docs/reconstructive-transform-v1.md L9-10

statement: Frozen v6 encoding pins one encoder thread and explicitly requests JPEG reconstruction data; jxl-oxide uses an allocation tracker with a 256 MiB limit.
research_needed: Verify jixel output is byte-deterministic across platforms/CPU features with one thread.

statement: The dependency boundary is governed by the transform registry; archive strings can only select registered jpeg-jxl-reconstruct/v1 behavior.
Canonical parameter bytes for jpeg-jxl-reconstruct/v1 are JJ01 NUL jixel-0.2.19 NUL jxl-oxide-0.12.6 NUL threads=1.
research_needed: Determine whether newer jxl-oxide versions reconstruct identically; parameters bind archives to library versions.
decision_needed: Must future readers keep jxl-oxide 0.12.6-compatible reconstruction forever to decode v6 archives?

statement: A ReconstructionRegion is one physical representation of a contiguous range of one ContentObject Chunk sequence, with fields region_id, content_object, start_chunk_index, chunk_count, transform_plan, logical/transformed/ordinary-physical/overhead byte counts, declared access cost, and encoded representation.
Region membership exists only as content_object + start_chunk_index + chunk_count; there is no serialized member list and ContentObject Chunk order remains the only logical order.
Version-3 CHUNK_DATA frames keep each original Chunk digest and logical length, set a region-owned flag, and contain no independent payload or plan.
Reader reconstructs the complete region, slices by authoritative logical lengths, and verifies every original Chunk SHA-256 digest.
Regions cannot overlap and a Chunk cannot have both an independent physical payload and region ownership.
research_needed: Negative corpus: overlapping regions, region-owned Chunk with payload.

statement: Multiple Entries may share a ContentObject, but v6 conservatively rejects a region if any member Chunk is referenced by a distinct ContentObject or already needs a Dictionary or ChunkGroup, preserving one physical representation per exact plaintext Chunk.
research_needed: Measure how often dedup/dictionary conflicts suppress JPEG regions on photo libraries with duplicates or edited copies.

statement: Recognition is byte-based: the complete ContentObject must have bounded conventional JPEG marker structure, at most 100,000,000 pixels, and at most 64 MiB original bytes.
Entrybound does not inspect filename extensions, decode pixels, or re-encode JPEG from pixel samples.

Every candidate runs original JPEG -> jixel JPEG XL -> jxl-oxide bitstream reconstruction -> recreated JPEG, requiring both SHA-256 and direct byte equality; failure rejects before planning and the ECF writer repeats the full check before commit; no opt-out.
The JPEG XL representation is self-contained, so the TransformStep has no ReconstructionData reference and no redundant side-data object is emitted.
The tested selected subset includes deterministic baseline sequential JPEGs.
research_needed: Test on real-camera and web JPEG corpora; report success rate and savings.

statement: APP/COM/EXIF/ICC marker arrangements are attempted when pinned libraries accept them and are eligible only if exact check succeeds; eligibility coverage is not quantified.
research_needed: Measure acceptance rate for marker-rich real-world JPEGs (camera EXIF, MPF, XMP, trailing data).

statement: The generated progressive corpus uses pure-Rust MIT-or-Apache-2.0 jpeg-encoder crate only as test tooling.
A known valid progressive producer output exposes an internal failure in the pinned JPEG/JPEG XL forward stack.
research_needed: Report upstream to jixel/jxl-oxide; reproduce minimal case.

statement: v1 rejects progressive SOF markers before entering the dependency and falls back; progressive JPEG is not part of the frozen v1 selected subset.
research_needed: Measure share of progressive JPEGs in web/photo corpora and savings forgone.
decision_needed: Should a later jpeg-jxl-reconstruct version (new planner ID) support progressive JPEG once the dependency is fixed?

statement: Dependency calls are unwind-confined.
research_needed: Verify release profile does not use panic=abort (which defeats unwind confinement) and that allocation-failure aborts are prevented by tracker.

statement: Some otherwise legal producer/marker combinations are rejected by v1 and fall back to ordinary v5 encoding; malformed, truncated, or unsupported inputs also fall back.
research_needed: Enumerate rejected legal combinations.

statement: Entrybound never weakens exactness for JPEG reconstruction.
Reconstruction is ContentObject-bounded: v6 does not scan nested JPEG streams (e.g., embedded thumbnails, JPEGs in containers) or span multiple ContentObjects.
research_needed: Measure JPEG content embedded in PDFs, office documents, ZIPs, and MPF files in target corpora.

statement: All v6 profiles retain corresponding frozen v5 CDC, exact dedup, independent codec/transform, similarity, Dictionary, and ChunkGroup behavior.
fast-v6 disables JPEG regions; no candidates.
balanced-v6 allows regions only for exactly one logical Chunk (lookback remains zero); post-codec candidates STORE, LZ4, Zstandard 3 and 5.
research_needed: Measure fraction of JPEGs that are a single CDC Chunk under balanced policy (files under ~128 KiB-2 MiB).

statement: dense-v6 allows complete eligible ContentObject regions up to 4096 Chunks; post-codec candidates STORE, Zstandard 9/15, LZMA2 preset 6 / 4 MiB.
extreme-v6 allows complete eligible ContentObject regions up to 4096 Chunks; post-codec candidates STORE, LZ4, Zstandard 15/19, LZMA2 6/4 MiB and 9/8 MiB.
Candidate ordering breaks equal complete costs in favor of the earlier/simpler representation.
balanced-v6 cannot select a multi-Chunk region, preserving independent-Chunk access by contract; dense and extreme may select whole-file regions with declared exact access cost.
Best post-codec representation is charged stored bytes, TransformPlan v3 bytes when newly required, the ReconstructionRegion record, and the region section header when first required.

Charging plan bytes 'when newly required' and section header 'when first required' makes a region's cost depend on evaluation order; the doc does not state the deterministic order of region evaluation.
research_needed: Inspect planner for region evaluation order; test permutation invariance of outputs.
decision_needed: Is order-dependent greedy costing acceptable, and is the order normatively fixed for v6?

statement: Existing Chunk frame and Index costs are common to both alternatives because original Chunk declarations remain, so the planner cancels equal terms.
research_needed: Verify version-3 region-owned frames are the same size as ordinary frames; otherwise cancellation is inexact.

statement: Baseline is the actual ordinary v5 payload set for unique member Chunks; a region must save strictly more than both 256 bytes and 2% of that baseline; ordinary representation wins ties.

Persisted audit records target a Chunk, ContentObject, or Region; v6 reasons: not recognized, implementation unsupported, exact verification failed, complete cost did not win, dedup/physical conflict, resource-policy exclusion.
Audits are physical planning evidence and never EAM semantic authority.
Every region declares logical bytes, logical Chunk count, and worst bytes needing reconstruction to access one member; v1 reconstructs the complete region so worst bytes equal region logical bytes.
research_needed: Measure random-access latency for large whole-file regions over HTTP range access.

statement: inspect reports the largest region, worst bytes/Chunks, and whether all content remains independently Chunk-decodable.

Frozen limits: original/reconstructed JPEG 64 MiB; JPEG XL and intermediate 64 MiB; region 4096 logical Chunks; 100,000,000 pixels; expansion 64:1; JPEG/JPEG XL working set 256 MiB; CLI aggregate decoder working-set policy 384 MiB.
evidence_in_source: none; limits chosen without cited measurement
research_needed: Measure jxl-oxide peak memory at 100M pixels vs 256 MiB tracker; check 384 MiB CLI default is compatible with low-memory devices.
decision_needed: Is a 384 MiB default CLI decoder working-set policy appropriate for constrained platforms?

statement: A 100,000,000-pixel JPEG could require more than the 256 MiB JPEG/JPEG XL working set; the doc does not state which limit binds or whether such images are rejected at recognition.
research_needed: Test 100M-pixel JPEG through jxl-oxide with tracker to observe behavior.

statement: Sizes and caller decode policy are checked before expensive decoding where available; the JXL allocation tracker and bounded reconstruction writer enforce limits during attacker-facing parsing.
research_needed: Fuzz jxl-oxide reconstruction path with hostile JPEG XL payloads under the tracker.

statement: Required incompatibility bit 0x8 (whole-object-reconstruction-v1) requires bits 0x1, 0x2, 0x4; selects TransformStep v3 records, adds authoritative RECONSTRUCTION_REGIONS section, and selects CHUNK_DATA frame version 3.
Feature bit 0x8 requires 0x4 (DEFLATE reconstruction) even though JPEG regions do not use ReconstructionData; each feature generation is cumulative rather than independently selectable.
decision_needed: Should feature bits remain a linear cumulative chain, or should independent features be composable for minimal readers?

statement: Historical v1-v5 records are not reinterpreted; readers that do not implement bit 0x8 fail closed.
Record type 17 is TransformStep v3 with fields transform identifier (1), parameters (2), optional ReconstructionData reference (3).
Record type 18 is ReconstructionRegion with fields listed in the whole-object model in order (1-13).
Type-18 is said to have fields 1-13 in whole-object-model order, but that model lists 11 items ('declared access cost' may span several fields); field numbering is ambiguous.
research_needed: Auditor spot-check: crates/entrybound/src/ecf/records.rs:643-656 encodes access fields as 8-10, representation 11, ordinary_physical_bytes 12, region_overhead_bytes 13, which differs from the doc's listing order; correct the normative field table.
decision_needed: Which is normative for type-18 field numbering, the doc listing or the implemented encoding?

statement: Record type 19 is ReconstructionAudit v2 with target kind (1), target digest (2), transform identifier (3), reason (4).
refines_or_supersedes: Extends type-16 ReconstructionFallback in docs/reconstructive-transform-v1.md L72-77

statement: Doc does not say whether v6 archives still emit type-16 fallback records for DEFLATE attempts or replace them with type-19, nor how explain handles both.
research_needed: Inspect writer and explain implementation for v6 audit emission.

statement: v6 extended section order: DESCRIPTOR, TRANSFORM_PLANS, DICTIONARIES, CHUNK_GROUPS, RECONSTRUCTION_DATA, RECONSTRUCTION_REGIONS, CHUNK_DATA, MANIFEST_RECORDS, FIDELITY, optional INDEX.
refines_or_supersedes: Extends docs/cross-file-compression-v1.md L94-99

statement: JPEG XL bytes, region identity/configuration, access declarations, and audits are physical facts; original Chunk digests, ContentObject logical digest, LAI, and AUX are unchanged; PCR unchanged if logical Chunk sequence unchanged; PCI changes when container bytes change.
A region is not verified until every reconstructed original member Chunk digest succeeds.
